analysis.title: Economics Week Ahead
key_insights: Wells Fargo expects the FOMC to hold rates at 4.00% (upper bound) at the Oct 28 meeting, despite Chair Warsh's hawkish rhetoric. They argue hiking does little against supply-side inflation, and a December hike remains the base case.

The FOMC meeting has no SEP or dot plot. Wells Fargo expects a short statement and little forward guidance in the press conference, with any lean likely hawkish. Attention may turn to the Chair's task forces, which were due to start reporting around the turn of the year.

The FOMC hiked 25 bps in September after Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole message. Wells Fargo says gradual hikes make more sense as catch-up to a higher neutral rate than as a response to supply-side inflation.

Wells Fargo forecasts September personal spending +0.6% m/m (about +0.1% real) and personal income +0.4%. It expects headline PCE +0.5% m/m (3.7% y/y) and core PCE +0.4% m/m (3.1% y/y), above consensus on the monthly core and headline y/y readings.

Q3 GDP first estimate is forecast at 3.2% annualized, driven by consumer spending (+3.4% real, annualized) and high-tech capex. Annual revisions showed household incomes grew faster than previously believed.

Housing is the weak spot. The 30-year mortgage rate passed 7.0% by end of September, builder sentiment is at its lowest since June 2012, and Wells Fargo forecasts September new home sales down 7.2% to 635K versus 650K consensus.

The Bank of Canada is expected to hold at 2.25%, but market pricing for a hike rose from ~30% to over 80% after Governor Macklem's comments. Wells Fargo thinks a hold is underappreciated, with risks tilted toward a hike. September CPI was 3.1% and core measures were little changed or lower.
Markets price about 100 bps of BoC tightening by end-2027. Wells Fargo calls that hard to justify and sees CAD vulnerable to near-term disappointment if data or the Bank fail to validate it.

The ECB is expected to hold the deposit rate at 2.50%, with France's fiscal and political turmoil lifting borrowing costs. September euro-area inflation is 3.8% headline and 2.5% core. December is the base case for the next hike, and a disorderly sovereign sell-off could derail it.
The BoJ is expected to hold at 1.25% after its last hike. September inflation is 2.1% headline and 2.4% on core-core. Wells Fargo expects a December hike and another in 2027 to 1.75%.

Mexico Q3 GDP is forecast at +1.1% q/q and +3.2% y/y, versus consensus of 0.4% and 2.3%. Wells Fargo expects Banxico to hold at 6.50% through 2026 and 2027 as headline inflation reached 3.62% in early October.
Tuesday's releases also include durable goods (WF +2.5% vs consensus 1.7%) and consumer confidence (WF 84.5 vs consensus 80.5). The Fed communications blackout runs through Oct 29.

risk_factors: A disorderly sell-off in French and other indebted Eurozone sovereign bonds could derail the ECB's December hike.
BoC may box itself into a hike after Macklem's hawkish comments, despite soft inflation and labor data.
Higher oil prices could spread cost pressures beyond energy.
Mortgage rates above 7.0% are weighing on housing demand.
Tariff escalation is a downside risk to Canadian growth into year-end.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price over 80% odds of an October hike and about 100 bps of tightening by end-2027, after Macklem's hawkish comments on oil and cost pass-through.
tension_points.bear_case: Wells Fargo sees September CPI at 3.1%, below expectations, core measures steady or lower, a softer labor market, and tariff risks to growth. It says a hold is underappreciated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A BoC hold, or data that fails to validate the hike pricing, would leave the Canadian dollar vulnerable to disappointment.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish rhetoric from Chair Warsh, a September hike, and hotter inflation argue for another hike, and December is the base case.
tension_points.bear_case: Wells Fargo argues hikes do little against supply-side inflation, and Fed speakers signaled a hold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hot September PCE and a hawkish press conference would reinforce the December hike.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed holds in October but a December hike is still the base case given hot inflation.
theme_stances.evidence: a December hike is still the base case
